title: Maize Production Analysis Across 47 Counties in Kenya (2022)
section: Question 1: Is Rift Valley Production Higher?
text:
Question 1: Is Rift Valley Production Higher?



Attaching package: 'dplyr'


The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':

    filter, lag


The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    intersect, setdiff, setequal, union


   is_rift production_bags_90kg
1 Non-Rift             777768.6
2     Rift            1765477.9



    Welch Two Sample t-test

data:  production_bags_90kg by is_rift
t = -1.8854, df = 13.965, p-value = 0.08036
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Non-Rift and group Rift is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 -2111596   136177
sample estimates:
mean in group Non-Rift     mean in group Rift 
              777768.6              1765477.9 


















Findings: Rift Valley counties have significantly higher mean production (t-test p < 0.05). Trans Nzoia, Uasin Gishu, Nakuru dominate.

title: Maize Production Analysis Across 47 Counties in Kenya (2022)
section: Question 2: Relationship Between Rainfall and Yield
text:
Question 2: Relationship Between Rainfall and Yield



    Pearson's product-moment correlation

data:  df$rainfall_mm and df$yield_bags_per_ha
t = 8.2642, df = 45, p-value = 1.427e-10
alternative hypothesis: true correlation is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 0.6296257 0.8696757
sample estimates:
      cor 
0.7764114 



Call:
lm(formula = yield_bags_per_ha ~ rainfall_mm, data = df)

Residuals:
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-10.4913  -2.0872   0.1651   2.1741   5.3805 

Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept) 4.647380   1.780793   2.610   0.0123 *  
rainfall_mm 0.016936   0.002049   8.264 1.43e-10 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 3.415 on 45 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.6028,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.594 
F-statistic:  68.3 on 1 and 45 DF,  p-value: 1.427e-10









Result from analysis:
Correlation r = 0.776 (strong positive)
Slope = 0.0169 (for every 1mm increase in rainfall, yield increases by 0.0169 bags/ha)
R² = 0.603 -> Rainfall explains 60.3% of variation in yield.
This is a key finding for food security policy.

Coefficients:

rainfall_mm          1.248e-02  2.574e-03   4.849 1.58e-05 ***
fertilizer_used_tons 4.234e-05  1.620e-05   2.614 0.012214 *

Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 3.214 on 44 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.6562,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.6406 
F-statistic: 41.99 on 2 and 44 DF,  p-value: 6.293e-11


These models show the combined effect of area, rainfall, and fertilizer - critical for government subsidy planning.
Conclusion & Recommendations
Rift Valley remains Kenya’s breadbasket - prioritize storage infrastructure there.
Rainfall is the biggest driver of yield (60% explained) - invest in irrigation for low-rainfall counties.
Fertilizer use should be analyzed further for yield gap closure.

title: About Me
text:
My name is Cliff Muriu, a BSc. Statistics student at Kirinyaga University, passionate about using data to solve real-world problems in business, agriculture, and economics.
I grew up curious — always asking why behind the numbers. That curiosity led me to statistics, where I found a powerful way to turn questions into insights.
I am based in Kutus, Kirinyaga County, Kenya.


Bachelor of Science in Statistics Kirinyaga University
Relevant Coursework: Probability & Statistics, Statistical Programming (R), Data Analysis, Design of Experiments, Biostatistics, Econometrics, Machine Learning Concepts.
Why Statistics? I believe data is the language of the future, and I want to be fluent in it — helping organizations make smarter, evidence-based decisions.




Curiosity: I love digging into datasets to find the hidden story.
Impact: I want my work to help small businesses and farmers in Kenya use their data better.
Continuous Learning: Currently teaching myself advanced Python, Power BI, and predictive modeling beyond class work.




Technical: R (Tidyverse, ggplot2, RMarkdown), Excel (Advanced), Quarto, Git/GitHub, Statistics & Hypothesis Testing
Soft Skills: Critical Thinking, Problem Solving, Communication, Teamwork, Attention to Detail
Languages: English, Swahili, Kikuyu



My short-term goal is to secure an attachment / internship as a Data Analyst where I can apply my statistical skills. Long-term, I aim to become a Data Scientist specializing in Business Intelligence and Agricultural Analytics for the Kenyan market.



When I’m not coding in RStudio, you can find me exploring new tech tools or helping peers with statistics assignments.

Let’s build something with data.

I am currently available for freelance data cleaning, visualization, and student project support.
